title: Democratic Midterm Sweep Fallout: Trump Blames Democrats, Data Center and SpaceX Pushback
summary: Gotrade News - President Donald Trump blamed Democrats for Thursday's sell-off on Nov. 5, when the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, according to Fox Business
body_markdown:
## Tesla (TSLA): Musk Companies Shed About $456 Billion by Thursday


[Tesla's slide began a day earlier](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/tesla-tsla-stock-news-november-5-2026/) , when the stock fell 3.5% in Wednesday premarket trading, per CNBC. By Thursday's close, SpaceX and Tesla had lost about $456 billion in combined market cap, CNBC reported, as investors weighed possible congressional probes and tighter regulation after the midterms.


Per CNBC, regulatory scrutiny could also block Musk's chances to merge SpaceX and Tesla, a deal that would first require shareholder approval. Musk spent at least $474 million on the midterms, including $224 million in Texas, according to CNBC's live coverage. Of 44 federal races targeted by his America PAC, Republicans it backed, or whose opponents it targeted, had lost 29 as of Wednesday morning, won three and were awaiting results in 12.


## Nvidia (NVDA): Voters Rejected 40 of 41 Data Center Measures


Data center pushback was on the ballot itself. Voters "resoundingly sided against the data center boom in 40 of the 41 measures under consideration" across 10 states, according to a Ballotpedia and CNBC analysis, with Harwood, North Dakota the only exception. Ohio held 21 local measures, residents of Ashville rejected a resolution that would have approved EdgeConneX data center terms, and voters in Joliet Township, Illinois, said no to a measure on AI data center construction, CNBC reported. Jim Bianco noted that the measures were non-binding.


Even as the Dow jumped more than 1,500 points on Wednesday, CoreWeave and Nebius each fell more than 7%, according to CNBC. On Thursday, Fox Business said tech and AI losses, including Nvidia, drove part of the sell-off as investors weighed the Democratic wins' potential effect on AI regulation and data center development. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell more than 12%, and investors also cited heavy AI-related borrowing and spending, rising energy costs and uncertain returns, Fox Business reported, in the Nasdaq's worst session since April 2025.
